name: p21 (RAC1) activated kinase 1

function.text: PAK1 encodes serine/threonine-protein kinase PAK 1. Annotated molecular activities include protein kinase activity and protein serine kinase activity. It participates in intracellular signal transduction and cell migration.

germline.text: Strong or definitive GenCC assertions link constitutional variants to intellectual developmental disorder with macrocephaly, seizures, and speech delay (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: This gene is included in cancer-panel definitions, but a disease-specific somatic association has not been assigned from the alteration-context sources reviewed for this draft.

germline_associations.mechanism: Autosomal dominant; strong GenCC assertion from Labcorp Genetics (formerly Invitae). Allele-specific mechanism requires review.

function.text: PAK1 encodes serine/threonine-protein kinase PAK 1. Based in part on similarity, it is a protein kinase involved in intracellular signaling pathways downstream of integrins and receptor-type kinases that plays an important role in cytoskeleton dynamics, in cell adhesion, migration, proliferation, apoptosis, mitosis, and in vesicle-mediated transport processes. It can directly phosphorylate BAD and protects cells against apoptosis. It acts as a GTPase effector that links the Rho-related GTPases CDC42 and RAC1 to the JNK MAP kinase pathway.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with intellectual developmental disorder with macrocephaly, seizures, and speech delay (autosomal dominant).
